groups.title: Eye drops (401637COS)
groups.efficacy: This is an over-the-counter medicine used for the relief of dryness of the eye and for the temporary relief of irritation.
groups.usage: Instil 1 to 2 drops into the eye as required. The amount may be increased or decreased as appropriate according to symptoms. After instillation, discard any solution that is left together with the container straight away.
groups.caution:
Use it for instillation into the eye only.
When instilling it, be careful that the opening of the container does not touch the eye directly.
To prevent contamination, avoid sharing it with other people as far as possible.
Do not use the solution if its colour has changed or if it has become cloudy.
Do not use it if the safety seal on the cap is broken.

If there is pain in the eye or a change in vision, continuing redness or a feeling of irritation, or if symptoms last for 72 hours or more, stop using it immediately and consult a doctor or pharmacist.

summaryTable.What it is for: Relief of dry eye symptoms and temporary relief of irritation

summaryTable.Ask the pharmacist: Ask the pharmacist in the store first if any of the cautions above apply to you.

groups.title: Oral liquid (D62800ALQ)
groups.efficacy: This is an over-the-counter medicine used to supply vitamin B6 in pregnancy and breast-feeding and when strength is reduced during or after an illness, and for the relief of muscle cramps caused by magnesium deficiency and of angular cheilitis (inflammation at the corners of the mouth), cheilitis (inflammation of the lips), stomatitis (inflammation inside the mouth), glossitis (inflammation of the tongue), eczema and dermatitis.
groups.usage: Adults and those aged 12 years and over: take 10 mL at a time, 2 times in 1 day, between meals.
groups.caution:
Do not take this medicine if you have hypersensitivity to it, if the user is a baby under 12 months of age, or if you have severe heart failure.
Before taking this medicine, consult a doctor or pharmacist if you have impaired heart or circulatory function, kidney disorder or a low protein level in the blood, if you are pregnant, or if you have hypersensitivity to caramel or have had it.
Keep to the stated dosage and schedule.
This medicine is for oral use only; do not use it for injection.

Do not take it together with phosphates, calcium salts, oral tetracycline preparations, antacids or levodopa.
Consult a doctor or pharmacist if you take it together with anti-aldosterone medicines or triamterene.
Avoid tea containing tannin, such as green tea and black tea, during the period of use and just before and after a dose.

If red patches, diarrhoea, cardiac arrest (stopping of the heartbeat) or reduced function of the central nervous system occurs, stop taking it immediately and consult a doctor or pharmacist.

summaryTable.What it is for: Vitamin B6 supply when strength is reduced, and relief of magnesium-deficiency muscle cramps, cheilitis, stomatitis, glossitis, eczema and dermatitis

groups.title: Cream (165138CCM)
groups.efficacy: This is an over-the-counter medicine used for primary skin infections (contagious impetigo, superficial folliculitis, ecthyma, boils, sycosis) and for secondary skin infections (infected eczema-like dermatitis, pustular psoriasis, seborrhoeic dermatitis and contact dermatitis with secondary infection by pus-forming bacteria, wounds and pustular acne, and mixed infection with a fungal or viral infection).
groups.usage: Apply to the affected area 1 to 4 times in 1 day and rub in gently. Gauze may be placed over it if needed. In contagious impetigo it is best to remove the crust first, taking care not to contaminate other normal skin, and then apply it.
groups.caution:
Do not use this medicine if you have hypersensitivity to it or to other aminoglycoside antibiotics (streptomycin, kanamycin, gentamicin, neomycin) or to bacitracin, or if the user is an infant under 1 year of age.
Before using this medicine, consult a doctor or pharmacist if you are pregnant, may be pregnant or are breast-feeding, or if you have had hypersensitivity or an allergic reaction to propylene glycol.
Use it only for the shortest period needed for treatment.
Do not use it for the eyes.

If excessive growth of insensitive organisms, skin irritation (erythema, itching and the like), a hypersensitivity reaction, a superimposed infection or signs of sensitisation (reddening, swelling, papules, small blisters) occurs, stop using it immediately and consult a doctor or pharmacist.

summaryTable.What it is for: Primary skin infections such as impetigo, folliculitis, ecthyma and boils, and secondary bacterial infection of eczema, psoriasis, dermatitis, wounds and acne

groups.title: Syrup (101342ASY)
groups.efficacy: This is an over-the-counter medicine used for fever and pain caused by a cold, headache, neuralgia, muscle pain, menstrual pain, the pain of a sprain, toothache, joint pain and rheumatic pain.
groups.usage: Children aged 12 years and under: take the recommended dose for the age at a time, every 4 to 6 hours as required. Take this medicine at the lowest effective dose for the shortest possible period, and do not take it more than 5 times in 1 day (75 mg/kg). For the dose for each age group, refer to the approved product information.
groups.caution:
If you regularly drink three or more glasses of alcohol every day, consult a doctor or pharmacist before taking this medicine or any other antipyretic analgesic. It may cause liver damage.
Very rarely, serious skin reactions that can be fatal — acute generalised exanthematous pustulosis, Stevens-Johnson syndrome and toxic epidermal necrolysis (Lyell's syndrome) — have been reported; if a skin rash or another sign of hypersensitivity appears after a dose of this medicine, stop taking it at once.
Do not go above the maximum daily amount of acetaminophen (4,000 mg). It may cause liver damage. Do not take it together with other products containing acetaminophen.

Do not take this medicine if you have hypersensitivity to it, peptic ulcer, a severe blood disorder, severe liver disorder, severe kidney disorder or severely reduced heart function; if you have aspirin asthma (an asthma attack brought on by non-steroidal anti-inflammatory medicines) or have had it; if you are taking barbiturates or tricyclic antidepressants; or if you have taken alcohol.
Before taking this medicine, consult a doctor or pharmacist if you have liver disorder or have had it, kidney disorder or have had it, a history of peptic ulcer, a blood disorder or have had one, a tendency to bleed, abnormal heart function or a history of hypersensitivity, bronchial asthma, if you are an older person, if the user is a child under 2 years of age, if you are pregnant or breast-feeding, or if you have been taking warfarin over a long period.

Before taking this medicine, consult a doctor or pharmacist if you have been taking lithium or thiazide diuretics.

If shock symptoms (difficulty breathing, reddening of the whole body, swelling of the blood vessels, hives and the like), an asthma attack, a fall in platelets, granulocytopenia, haemolytic anaemia (destruction of red cells), methaemoglobinaemia, reduced platelet function (prolonged bleeding time), cyanosis, hypersensitivity symptoms (facial swelling, difficulty breathing, sweating, low blood pressure), nausea, vomiting, loss of appetite, gastrointestinal effects such as gastrointestinal bleeding, peptic ulcer or perforation with long-term use, rash, an allergic reaction, Stevens-Johnson syndrome, toxic epidermal necrolysis (Lyell's syndrome), a rise in AST, a rise in ALT or a fixed drug eruption occurs, stop taking it immediately and consult a doctor or pharmacist.
If pain or fever lasts or gets worse, or if new symptoms appear, consult a doctor or pharmacist.

summaryTable.What it is for: Fever and pain from a cold, headache, neuralgia, muscle pain, menstrual pain, sprain pain, toothache, joint pain and rheumatic pain

groups.title: Capsule (228202ACH)
groups.efficacy: This is an over-the-counter medicine used for acute and chronic disorders of the airways in which secretion is increased, such as acute and chronic bronchitis, bronchitis with breathing difficulty (asthma, cough), nasopharyngitis and laryngotracheitis.
groups.usage: Adults: take 1 capsule (200 mg) at a time, 2 times in 1 day.
groups.caution:
Do not take this medicine if you have hypersensitivity to it, or if you have a hereditary problem such as galactose intolerance, Lapp lactase deficiency or glucose-galactose malabsorption. Before taking this medicine, consult a doctor or pharmacist if you are pregnant, may be pregnant or are breast-feeding, or if the user is an infant under 2 years of age.

If a generalised allergic reaction (reddening of the skin, itching, a burning sensation) or a local reaction rarely occurs, stop taking it immediately and consult a doctor or pharmacist.

groups.title: Enteric-coated tablet (A27400ATE)
groups.efficacy: This is an over-the-counter medicine used for constipation and for the relief of the loss of appetite (reduced appetite), abdominal (belly) bloating, abnormal fermentation in the bowel and haemorrhoids that accompany constipation.
groups.usage: Those aged 15 years and over: take 2 tablets at a time. Those aged 11 years and over but under 15 years: take 1 1/3 tablets at a time. Those aged 8 years and over but under 11 years: take 1 tablet at a time. Take it 1 time in 1 day at bedtime. For the first dose take the smallest amount, and then increase or decrease it little by little while watching the form and condition of the stool.
groups.caution:
Children aged 7 years and under, and people with an acute abdominal disease (appendicitis, intestinal bleeding, ulcerative colitis and the like), intestinal obstruction (blocked bowel), or a hereditary problem such as galactose intolerance, Lapp lactase deficiency or glucose-galactose malabsorption, must not take this medicine. Before taking this medicine, consult a doctor or pharmacist if you are pregnant or may be pregnant, if the user is a child aged 10 years or under, if you have severe abdominal pain, nausea or vomiting, or if you have had rectal bleeding or bowel failure. Keep to the stated dosage and schedule. If constipation does not improve after about 1 week of use, stop taking it and consult a doctor or pharmacist. When it is given to a child, give it under the guidance and supervision of a guardian. Do not chew the tablet.

Do not take it together with antacids. Avoid taking it within 1 hour after drinking milk.

If rash or reddening, itching, severe abdominal pain, diarrhoea, vomiting, abdominal discomfort or cramping occurs, stop taking it immediately and consult a doctor or pharmacist.

summaryTable.What it is for: Constipation, and the loss of appetite, abdominal bloating, abnormal intestinal fermentation and haemorrhoids that accompany it

groups.title: Soft capsule (246501ACS)
groups.efficacy: This is an over-the-counter medicine used as supportive treatment for liver disease and for disease of the biliary system (the bile ducts and the gallbladder) arising from insufficient secretion of bile, to improve liver function in chronic liver disease, and for indigestion after removal of part of the small bowel and in inflammatory disease of the small bowel.
groups.usage: Take 1/2 to 1 capsule (50 mg to 100 mg as ursodeoxycholic acid) at a time, 3 times in 1 day.
groups.caution:
Do not take this medicine if you have hypersensitivity to it, severe obstruction of the bile duct, fulminant hepatitis, radio-opaque calcified gallstones or a non-functioning gallbladder; if you are pregnant, may be pregnant or are breast-feeding; if the user is a child; if you have kidney disease, peptic ulcer (acute gastric or duodenal ulcer), or inflammation of the large or small bowel such as Crohn's disease; or if you are hypersensitive to soya, peanut or soya-bean oil or have a history of allergy to them.
Before taking this medicine, consult a doctor or pharmacist if you have a disorder of fat metabolism such as hyperlipoproteinaemia, diabetic hyperlipidaemia or pancreatitis, or if fat emulsions must be given to you with care; if you have hypersensitivity to Food Yellow No. 5 or have had it; if you have severe disease of the pancreas; if you have gallstones in the bile duct; if you have bleeding from varices, hepatic coma or ascites (fluid in the abdomen); if you may suddenly need a liver transplant; or if fat overload would place you at particular risk.

Consult a doctor or pharmacist if you take it together with oral medicines for diabetes (tolbutamide), cholestyramine, colestipol, medicinal charcoal, antacids containing magnesium and aluminium hydroxide, medicines that increase the secretion of cholesterol from the liver (for example oral contraceptives containing oestrogen, or lipid-lowering medicines such as clofibrate), or medicines that damage the liver.

If diarrhoea, nausea, vomiting or itching occurs from time to time, or rarely abdominal pain, constipation, heartburn, stomach discomfort, rash, fever, cough, difficulty breathing, interstitial pneumonia with an abnormal chest X-ray, generalised malaise, dizziness, calcification of gallstones, a rise in liver enzymes (ALT, ALP, AST, GT) or a fall in white cells, stop taking it immediately and consult a doctor or pharmacist.

summaryTable.What it is for: Supportive treatment of liver and biliary disease from insufficient bile, liver function in chronic liver disease, and indigestion after small-bowel surgery or in inflammatory small-bowel disease

groups.title: Eye drops (B93700COS)
groups.efficacy: This is an over-the-counter medicine used for tired eyes, redness of the conjunctiva, prevention of eye disease (discomfort of the eye after swimming, or when dust or sweat has got into the eye), inflammation of the eye caused by ultraviolet and other light, soreness of the eyelids, discomfort when hard contact lenses are worn, itching of the eye, and blurring of the eye (for example when there is a lot of eye discharge).
groups.usage: Instil 1 to 3 drops into the eye at a time, 3 to 6 times in 1 day.
groups.caution:
Infants aged 30 months and under must not use this medicine.
Before using this medicine, consult a doctor or pharmacist if you have severe pain in the eye, if you have had an allergy to an eye medicine, if you have an allergic constitution, if you have glaucoma, or if the user is a child.
Use this medicine for instillation into the eye only.
Keep to the stated dosage and schedule.
When it is used for a child, use it under the guidance and supervision of a guardian.
Do not use it as a wetting solution for soft contact lenses, and do not use it while soft contact lenses are being worn.
To prevent contamination, avoid sharing it with other people as far as possible.
Do not use it after the expiry date, and once it has been opened use it as soon as possible.

If redness of the eye, itching or swelling occurs, or a skin rash, or if blurring of the eye does not improve, stop using it immediately and consult a doctor or pharmacist.

summaryTable.What it is for: Tired eyes, conjunctival redness, eye inflammation from light, sore eyelids, itching and blurring, and prevention of eye trouble after swimming or exposure to dust

groups.title: Tablet (E28800ATB)
groups.efficacy: This is an over-the-counter medicine used for constipation and for the relief of the loss of appetite (reduced appetite), abdominal bloating, abnormal fermentation in the bowel and haemorrhoids that follow constipation.
groups.usage: Adults: take 1 to 2 tablets at a time, 1 time in 1 day, at bedtime (or on an empty stomach). For the first dose take the smallest amount, and then increase or decrease it little by little while watching the form and condition of the stool.
groups.caution:
Do not take this medicine if you have an acute abdominal disease (appendicitis, intestinal bleeding, ulcerative colitis and the like), intestinal obstruction (blocked bowel), or a hereditary problem such as galactose intolerance, Lapp lactase deficiency or glucose-galactose malabsorption.
Before taking this medicine, consult a doctor or pharmacist if you are pregnant or may be pregnant, if the user is a child aged 10 years or under, if you have an allergic constitution, severe abdominal pain, nausea or vomiting, or if you have had rectal bleeding or bowel failure.
Keep to the stated dosage and schedule.
Do not chew the tablet.
If there is no improvement in symptoms after about 1 week of use, stop taking it immediately and consult a doctor or pharmacist.

Do not take it together with antacids.
Do not take this medicine within 1 hour after drinking milk.

If rash, reddening, itching, severe abdominal pain, diarrhoea, vomiting, abdominal discomfort or cramping occurs, stop taking it immediately and consult a doctor or pharmacist.

groups.title: Cream (658500CCM)
groups.efficacy: This is an over-the-counter medicine used for the early treatment of recurrent cold sores of the lip (herpes labialis).
groups.usage: Adults: use an amount large enough to cover the affected area right up to its edge, 5 times in 1 day, for 5 days. Limit the treatment period with this medicine to 5 days or less. Start treatment as soon as possible, as soon as the first symptoms and signs appear.
groups.caution:
Do not use this medicine if you have hypersensitivity to it; if you have a skin infection (tuberculosis, syphilis, candidiasis, ringworm, shingles, chickenpox, vaccinia, scabies, pubic lice); if your immune system is damaged (bone-marrow transplant or AIDS); if you have eczematous otitis externa with a perforated eardrum, an ulcer (except in Behçet's disease), a deep second-degree or worse burn or frostbite, dermatitis around the mouth, common acne or rosacea; if you are breast-feeding; if the user is under 18 years of age; or if you have or have had a myocardial infarction.
Before using this medicine, consult a doctor or pharmacist if you are pregnant or may be pregnant, or if you are an older person.
Keep to the stated dosage and schedule.
Use it only for cold sores on the lips or around the mouth; do not use it in the eyes, the nose, the mouth or on the genitals.
Do not use it in people who have no signs or symptoms.
Do not use it to prevent infection of other people or to prevent recurrent herpes simplex infection.
Do not use this medicine as a base for diluting or mixing other medicines.

Consult a doctor or pharmacist if you use it together with probenecid.

Dryness and peeling of the skin occur commonly, and a temporary burning sensation or numbness occurs from time to time. If erythema, pigmentation, a reaction at the site of application including signs and symptoms of inflammation, contact dermatitis, contagious impetigo, folliculitis, candidiasis, ringworm, a boil, skin irritation, stinging pain, fever, a burning sensation, rash, reddening, flushing, itching, dry skin, pustular dermatitis, allergic contact dermatitis, prickly heat, sweat rash, worsening of a wound, a pressure sore or pustules occurs, or if raised pressure inside the eye or glaucoma (blurred vision, impaired sight) occurs when it is used on the skin of the eyelid, stop using it immediately and consult a doctor or pharmacist. Absorption into the body may cause reversible Cushing's syndrome, a high blood sugar level, sugar in the urine and visual disturbance.

groups.title: Oral liquid (158632ALQ)
groups.efficacy: This is an over-the-counter medicine used for iron deficiency anaemia.
groups.usage: Adults: take 1 bottle (100 mg as iron), 1 time in 1 day. Children aged 12 years and over but under 19 years: take 1/2 bottle (50 mg as iron) at a time, 2 times in 1 day. Children aged 1 year and over but under 12 years: take 1/2 bottle (50 mg as iron) at a time, 1 to 2 times in 1 day. Take it before a meal, during a meal or after a meal.
groups.caution:
An overdose in a child aged 6 years or under can cause fatal iron poisoning, so keep it out of the reach of children.

Do not take this medicine if you have hypersensitivity to it; if the user is an infant under 12 months of age; if you have haemochromatosis (a disease in which iron is deposited in the liver and pancreas because of abnormal iron metabolism), haemosiderosis, anaemia that is not due to iron deficiency, a disorder of iron use, iron overload, anaemia due to bone-marrow failure, chronic haemolytic anaemia, iron deficiency anaemia due to infection or tumour, chronic pancreatitis or cirrhosis of the liver.
Before taking this medicine, consult a doctor or pharmacist if you have a gastrointestinal disease such as peptic ulcer, chronic ulcerative colitis or regional colitis, impaired heart or circulatory function, paroxysmal nocturnal haemoglobinuria, kidney disorder, or a low protein level in the blood.
Keep to the stated dosage and schedule.
When it is given to a child, give it under the guidance and supervision of a guardian.

Do not take it together with phosphates, calcium salts, oral tetracycline antibiotics or antacids. Consult a doctor or pharmacist if you take it together with iron-containing preparations (iron supplements, liver contrast agents for MRI and the like), anti-aldosterone medicines, triamterene, diphosphonates, thyroxine, cefdinir preparations, quinolones, penicillamine, cholestyramine, pancreatic extract, preparations such as vitamin E, or 200 mg or more of ascorbic acid (vitamin C). Avoid tea containing tannin, such as green tea and black tea, and milk and dairy products, during the period of use and just before and after a dose.

If hives, itching, a hypersensitivity reaction of the skin on exposure to sunlight, abdominal or stomach pain, stomach cramps, vomiting, diarrhoea, fever or coma occurs, or from time to time a rise in AST and ALT, or rarely a rise in ALP, nausea, loss of appetite, constipation, black stools, discoloration of the teeth or stomach discomfort, stop taking it immediately and consult a doctor or pharmacist.

groups.title: Lotion (340100CLT)
groups.efficacy: This is an over-the-counter medicine used for pain relief and the reduction of inflammation in sprains, bruises, muscle pain, joint pain, fracture pain, back pain, stiff shoulders, neuralgia, rheumatic pain, itching of the skin, insect bites and chilblains.
groups.usage: Apply an appropriate amount to the affected area 1 to 4 times in 1 day.
groups.caution:
Do not use this medicine around the eyes, on mucous membranes, on eczema, on dermatitis caused by lacquer and the like, on wounds, or on sensitive skin.
Before using this medicine, consult a doctor or pharmacist if you have had allergic symptoms caused by a medicine or a cosmetic, if you have an allergic constitution, if the skin is very moist or badly broken down, if you have a circulatory disorder or diabetes, if the user is a child aged 12 years or under, or if you are pregnant, may be pregnant or are breast-feeding.
Keep to the stated dosage and schedule.
When it is used for a child, use it under the guidance and supervision of a guardian.
This medicine is for external use only; it must not be swallowed.
Be careful that it does not get into the eyes, and if it does, wash it out with water at once.
Do not wrap or bandage the treated area, and do not expose it to outside heat or hot water.
If there is no improvement in symptoms after 5 or 6 days of use, stop using it immediately and consult a doctor or pharmacist.

If rash or reddening or itching occurs, stop using it immediately and consult a doctor or pharmacist.

groups.title: Syrup (B89400ASY)
groups.efficacy: This is an over-the-counter medicine used for the relief of the various symptoms of a cold (runny nose, blocked nose, sneezing, sore throat (pain in the throat), cough, phlegm, chills, fever, headache, joint pain, muscle pain).
groups.usage: Adults and those aged 15 years and over: take 30 mL at a time. Those aged 11 years and over but under 15 years: take 20 mL at a time. Those aged 7 years and over but under 11 years: take 15 mL at a time. Those aged 3 years and over but under 7 years: take 10 mL at a time. Those aged 2 years and over but under 3 years: take 7.5 mL at a time. Take it after every meal and, if needed, at bedtime. As a rule, leave an interval of 4 hours between doses.
groups.caution:
If you regularly drink three or more glasses of alcohol every day, consult a doctor or pharmacist before taking this medicine or any other antipyretic analgesic. It may cause liver damage. Very rarely, serious skin reactions that can be fatal — acute generalised exanthematous pustulosis, Stevens-Johnson syndrome and toxic epidermal necrolysis — have been reported; if a skin rash or another sign of hypersensitivity appears after a dose of this medicine, stop taking it at once. Do not go above the maximum daily amount of acetaminophen (4,000 mg). It may cause liver damage. Do not take it together with other products containing acetaminophen.

Do not take this medicine if you have hypersensitivity to it or have had it, if you have had asthma when taking another antipyretic analgesic or cold medicine, if the user is an infant under 3 months of age, or if you are taking an MAO inhibitor (antidepressant, antipsychotic, mood stabiliser, anti-Parkinson medicine and the like) or stopped taking one within the last 2 weeks. Before taking this medicine, consult a doctor or pharmacist if the user is an infant or a child under 15 years of age who has, or is suspected of having, chickenpox or influenza; if the user is an infant aged 3 months and over but under 2 years; if you are pregnant, may be pregnant or are breast-feeding; if you are an older person or physically weak; if you have an allergic constitution or have had allergic symptoms (fever, rash, joint pain, asthma, itching and the like); if you have liver disease, kidney disease, heart disease, thyroid disease, diabetes, high blood pressure, gastric or duodenal ulcer, glaucoma (eye pain, blurred vision and the like) or difficulty passing urine; if you have a high fever, heartburn, stomach discomfort, stomach pain or another stomach problem, an ulcer or a bleeding problem; or if you smoke, or have asthma, chronic bronchitis, emphysema, a cough with a lot of phlegm, a cough lasting or coming back for more than 1 week, a chronic cough, or a cough with fever, rash or a persistent headache. Keep to the stated dosage and schedule. When it is given to a child, give it under the guidance and supervision of a guardian. Drowsiness may occur after a dose, so be careful when driving or operating machinery.

Do not take it together with other products containing acetaminophen, MAO inhibitors (antidepressants, antipsychotics, mood stabilisers, anti-Parkinson medicines and the like), cough and expectorant medicines, other cold medicines, antipyretic analgesics, sedatives, or oral medicines containing antihistamines (oral medicines for rhinitis, travel sickness medicines, allergy medicines). Consult a doctor or pharmacist if you take it together with medicines for diabetes, gout or arthritis, anticoagulants, steroids, barbiturates, tricyclic antidepressants or alcohol. Do not drink alcohol while you are taking it.

If rash, reddening, itching, nausea, vomiting, loss of appetite, constipation, oedema (swelling), difficulty passing urine, thirst (persistent or severe), dizziness, anxiety, tremor, insomnia, shock (hives, swelling and tightness of the chest immediately after a dose, together with pallor, cold hands and feet, cold sweat and difficulty breathing), Stevens-Johnson syndrome, toxic epidermal necrolysis (severe symptoms with high fever, and a rash or reddening with burn-like blisters, on the skin of the whole body and on the mucous membranes of the mouth or eyes), acute generalised exanthematous pustulosis, asthma, generalised weakness, jaundice or interstitial pneumonia (cough with shortness of breath, difficulty breathing and fever) occurs, stop taking it immediately and consult a doctor or pharmacist.

groups.title: Tablet (A14400ATB)
groups.efficacy: This is an over-the-counter medicine used for contraception.
groups.usage: Take 1 tablet in 1 day for 21 days in the order marked on the pack, and then have 7 days without tablets. It is best to take it at the same time every day where possible. Menstruation occurs during the 7 tablet-free days and usually starts within 2 to 3 days after the last tablet. If you go on with this medicine, start the tablets from a new pack after the 7 tablet-free days; menstruation may not have finished before the new pack is started. For details such as what to do if a dose is missed or if the cycle is to be changed, refer to the detailed approved product information.
groups.caution:
The risk of serious cardiovascular events such as thrombosis may be increased, so women taking an oral contraceptive should not smoke. Smokers aged 35 years and over must not take this medicine.

Do not take this medicine if you have hypersensitivity to it; if you have or have had an oestrogen-dependent tumour (for example breast cancer, cancer of the lining of the womb); if you have or have had thrombotic arteritis or phlebitis or thromboembolism, deep vein thrombosis, or an inherited or acquired tendency to thrombosis; if you have cerebrovascular or coronary artery disease (in particular myocardial infarction); if you are at high risk of venous or arterial thrombosis; if you have abnormal genital bleeding that has not been diagnosed; if you have moderate or severe high blood pressure, moderate or severe liver disorder, Dubin-Johnson syndrome or Rotor syndrome, jaundice, cholestasis, hepatitis or a benign or malignant liver tumour; if you have sickle cell anaemia; if you have a severe metabolic disorder such as severe diabetes with damage to the blood vessels, severe hyperlipidaemia, hyperlipoproteinaemia or porphyria; if you have had persistent itching in pregnancy, herpes gestationis, pemphigoid gestationis or otosclerosis; if you are pregnant, may be pregnant or are breast-feeding; if you have a pituitary tumour or a high prolactin level that may be accompanied by discharge of milk; if you have migraine with warning symptoms such as scintillating scotoma or fortification spectra; if you have valvular heart disease with pulmonary hypertension or atrial fibrillation; if you have had subacute bacterial endocarditis; if you have valvular heart disease; if you have diabetes with damage to the blood vessels (diabetic kidney disease, diabetic retinopathy and the like); if you have a history of pancreatitis or of severe hypertriglyceridaemia; if you have headache with focal neurological symptoms such as an aura; if you are receiving a direct-acting antiviral medicine for hepatitis C; if you are a smoker aged 35 years and over; or if you have a hereditary problem such as galactose intolerance, Lapp lactase deficiency or glucose-galactose malabsorption.
Before taking this medicine, consult a doctor or pharmacist if you are a woman aged 40 years and over; if you have epilepsy; if you have had breast cancer; if you have or have had depression; if you have heart or kidney failure; if you have atypical hyperplastic breast disease; if you have had a breast lump; if you have had hyperlipidaemia; if you have had gallbladder disease or gallstones; if you have endometriosis, asthma or melasma; if you have a disorder of the peripheral circulation; or if you have severe gastrointestinal disorder.
This medicine does not protect against HIV infection (AIDS) or other sexually transmitted infections.
This medicine is not for use in girls before their first period or in women after the menopause.
Keep to the stated dosage and schedule.

Do not take it together with direct-acting antiviral medicines for hepatitis C, grapefruit juice, phenytoin, barbiturates, primidone, carbamazepine, rifampicin, rufinamide, aprepitant, bosentan, efavirenz, lipid-lowering medicines or antibiotics.

If thrombophlebitis, arterial thromboembolism, venous thromboembolism, stroke, bleeding in the brain, blockage of a blood vessel, myocardial infarction, pulmonary embolism, a rise in blood pressure, worsening of varicose veins, bleeding between periods (spotting, breakthrough bleeding), a change in the amount of menstrual blood, absence of periods, a change in vaginal discharge, an increase in the size of a fibroid, cervical erosion, vaginal candidiasis, vaginitis, premenstrual syndrome, haemolytic uraemic syndrome, painful periods, breast tension and enlargement, discharge of milk, breast pain, benign breast disease, breast tenderness, discharge from the breast, nausea, vomiting, a feeling of abdominal bloating, abdominal cramps, gastrointestinal disturbance, secretion of bile, hepatitis without jaundice, cholestatic jaundice, a malignant or benign liver tumour, gallbladder disease, headache, migraine, depression, dizziness, nervousness, chorea, epilepsy, reduced perception, collapse, a disorder of accommodation, mood change, persistence of melasma, acne, erythema multiforme, erythema nodosum, worsening of systemic lupus erythematosus, a bleeding or allergic rash, oedema, itching, hives, seborrhoea, excess hair growth, hair loss, rash, visual disturbance, a change in the refractive power of the cornea, altered tolerance of contact lenses, retinal thrombosis, optic neuritis, hearing impairment, retention of sodium and body fluid, reduced glucose tolerance, diabetes, a high triglyceride level, a high cholesterol level, a change in weight, a change in appetite, a change in sexual desire, a speech disorder or, rarely, a prolactin-secreting pituitary tumour occurs, stop taking it immediately and consult a doctor or pharmacist. These are the usual side effects of contraceptives; for details refer to the approved product information.

groups.title: Tablet (A78000ATB)
groups.efficacy: This is an over-the-counter medicine used to supply vitamins B1, B6 and B12 in physical tiredness, in pregnancy and breast-feeding and when strength is reduced during or after an illness, and for the relief of neuralgia, muscle pain, joint pain (back pain, stiff shoulders, frozen shoulder and the like), numbness of the hands and feet, and tired eyes.
groups.usage: Children aged 15 years and over and adults: take 2 to 3 tablets at a time. Children aged 11 to 14 years: take 1 to 2 tablets at a time. Children aged 5 to 10 years: take 1 tablet at a time. Take it 1 time in 1 day.
groups.caution:
Do not take this medicine if you have hypersensitivity to it, if the user is a child under 5 years of age, or if you have a hereditary problem such as galactose intolerance, Lapp lactase deficiency or glucose-galactose malabsorption. Before taking this medicine, consult a doctor or pharmacist if you are pregnant or breast-feeding, if you have a tendency to thrombosis, or if you are short of folic acid. Keep to the stated dosage and schedule. When it is given to a child, give it under the guidance and supervision of a guardian. Do not handle this medicine with wet hands, as the tablet may become discoloured.

Do not take it together with levodopa. Consult a doctor or pharmacist if you take it together with an oral contraceptive containing oestrogen.

If rash or reddening, itching, nausea or vomiting, stomach discomfort, loss of appetite, a feeling of abdominal bloating, loose stools, diarrhoea or constipation lasts or gets worse, or if a period comes earlier than expected, the amount of bleeding gradually increases, or bleeding lasts a long time, stop taking it immediately and consult a doctor or pharmacist.

groups.title: Tablet (E62700ATB)
groups.efficacy: This is an over-the-counter medicine used for the relief of the various symptoms of a cold (sore throat, cough, phlegm, chills, fever, headache, joint pain, muscle pain).
groups.usage: Adults and those aged 15 years and over: take 2 tablets at a time, 3 times in 1 day, 30 minutes after meals.
groups.caution:
If you regularly drink three or more glasses of alcohol every day, consult a doctor or pharmacist before taking this medicine or any other antipyretic analgesic. It may cause liver damage.
Very rarely, serious skin reactions that can be fatal — acute generalised exanthematous pustulosis, Stevens-Johnson syndrome and toxic epidermal necrolysis — have been reported; if a skin rash or another sign of hypersensitivity appears after a dose of this medicine, stop taking it at once.
Do not go above the maximum daily amount of acetaminophen (4,000 mg). It may cause liver damage. Do not take it together with other products containing acetaminophen.

Do not take this medicine if you have hypersensitivity to it, if you have had asthma when taking another antipyretic analgesic or cold medicine, if the user is an infant under 3 months of age or a child under 2 years of age, if you are taking an MAO inhibitor (antidepressant, antipsychotic, mood stabiliser, anti-Parkinson medicine and the like) or stopped taking one within the last 2 weeks, or if you have a hereditary problem such as galactose intolerance, Lapp lactase deficiency or glucose-galactose malabsorption.
Before taking this medicine, consult a doctor or pharmacist if the user is an infant or a child under 15 years of age who has, or is suspected of having, chickenpox or influenza; if you have an allergic constitution or have had allergic symptoms (fever, rash, joint pain, asthma, itching and the like); if you have liver disease, kidney disease, heart disease, thyroid disease, diabetes, high blood pressure or gastric or duodenal ulcer; if you are an older person, physically weak or have a high fever; if you have heartburn, stomach discomfort, stomach pain or another stomach problem, an ulcer or a bleeding problem; if you are pregnant, may be pregnant or are breast-feeding; if you smoke, or have asthma, chronic bronchitis, emphysema, a cough with a lot of phlegm, a cough lasting or coming back for more than 1 week, a chronic cough, or a cough with fever, rash or a persistent headache; or if you have had hypersensitivity or an allergic reaction to Food Yellow No. 4.
Keep to the stated dosage and schedule.
If there is no improvement in symptoms after about 5 or 6 doses, stop taking it immediately and consult a doctor or pharmacist.

Do not take it together with MAO inhibitors (antidepressants, antipsychotics, mood stabilisers, anti-Parkinson medicines and the like), cough and expectorant medicines, other cold medicines, antipyretic analgesics, sedatives, or oral medicines containing antihistamines (oral medicines for rhinitis, travel sickness medicines, allergy medicines).
Consult a doctor or pharmacist if you are receiving medicines for diabetes, gout or arthritis, anticoagulants or steroids.
Do not drink alcohol while you are taking it.

If rash or reddening, itching, nausea or vomiting, loss of appetite, constipation, oedema (swelling), dizziness, anxiety, tremor, insomnia, shock symptoms (hives, tightness of the chest and the like), Stevens-Johnson syndrome, toxic epidermal necrolysis (Lyell's syndrome), asthma, generalised weakness, jaundice or interstitial pneumonia (cough with shortness of breath, difficulty breathing and fever) occurs, stop taking it immediately and consult a doctor or pharmacist.

groups.title: Tablet (D12600ATB)
groups.efficacy: This is an over-the-counter medicine used for the relief of the various symptoms of a cold (sore throat, cough, phlegm, chills, fever, headache, joint pain, muscle pain).
groups.usage: Adults and those aged 15 years and over: take 1 tablet at a time, 3 times in 1 day, 30 minutes after meals. Leave an interval of 4 hours between doses.
groups.caution:
If you regularly drink three or more glasses of alcohol every day, consult a doctor or pharmacist before taking this medicine or any other antipyretic analgesic. It may cause liver damage.
Very rarely, serious skin reactions that can be fatal — acute generalised exanthematous pustulosis, Stevens-Johnson syndrome and toxic epidermal necrolysis — have been reported; if a skin rash or another sign of hypersensitivity appears after a dose of this medicine, stop taking it at once.
Do not go above the maximum daily amount of acetaminophen (4,000 mg). It may cause liver damage. Do not take it together with other products containing acetaminophen.

Do not take this medicine if you have hypersensitivity to it, if you have had asthma when taking another antipyretic analgesic or cold medicine, if the user is an infant under 3 months of age, if you are taking an MAO inhibitor (antidepressant, antipsychotic, mood stabiliser, anti-Parkinson medicine and the like) or stopped taking one within the last 2 weeks, or if you have a hereditary problem such as galactose intolerance, Lapp lactase deficiency or glucose-galactose malabsorption.
Before taking this medicine, consult a doctor or pharmacist if the user is an infant or a child under 15 years of age who has, or is suspected of having, chickenpox or influenza; if you have an allergic constitution or have had allergic symptoms caused by a medicine (fever, rash, joint pain, asthma, itching and the like); if you have liver, kidney, heart or thyroid disease, diabetes, high blood pressure or gastric or duodenal ulcer; if you are an older person, physically weak or have a high fever; if you have heartburn, stomach discomfort, stomach pain or another stomach problem that lasts or comes back, or an ulcer or a bleeding problem; or if you are pregnant, may be pregnant or are breast-feeding.
Keep to the stated dosage and schedule.
If there is no improvement in symptoms after 5 or 6 doses, stop taking it immediately and consult a doctor or pharmacist.

Do not take it together with cough and expectorant medicines, other cold medicines, antipyretic analgesics, sedatives, or oral medicines containing antihistamines (oral medicines for rhinitis, travel sickness medicines, allergy medicines).
Consult a doctor or pharmacist if you take it together with medicines for diabetes, gout or arthritis, anticoagulants, steroids, barbiturates, tricyclic antidepressants or alcohol.
Do not drink alcohol while you are taking it.

If rash or reddening, itching, nausea or vomiting, loss of appetite, constipation, oedema, dizziness, anxiety, tremor or insomnia occurs, or rarely shock (hives, swelling and tightness of the chest immediately after a dose, together with pallor, cold hands and feet, cold sweat and difficulty breathing), Stevens-Johnson syndrome, toxic epidermal necrolysis (Lyell's syndrome — severe symptoms with high fever, and a rash or reddening with burn-like blisters), asthma, generalised weakness, jaundice (yellowing of the skin or the whites of the eyes) or interstitial pneumonia (cough with shortness of breath, difficulty breathing and fever), stop taking it immediately and consult a doctor or pharmacist.

groups.title: Cream (D64300CCM)
groups.efficacy: This is an over-the-counter medicine used for acne and spots.
groups.usage: After washing the face with soap or something similar, apply an appropriate amount to the affected area several times in 1 day.
groups.caution:
Do not use this medicine if you have hypersensitivity to it or if you are pregnant.
Do not use it in or around the eyes.
Before using this medicine, consult a doctor or pharmacist if you are pregnant (first or second trimester) and it is genuinely needed, if you have a history of allergic symptoms caused by a medicine or a cosmetic, if the skin is very moist or badly broken down, or if you have hypersensitivity to propylene glycol or have had it.
Use it only on the areas with acne or spots, and not over a wide surrounding area or around the eyes.
Be careful that it does not get into the eyes, and if it does, wash it out at once with water or lukewarm water.
Use this medicine externally only.
Keep to the stated dosage and schedule.
Be careful not to let it touch skin other than the area being treated.

If local skin irritation (for example rash with reddening, itching, dryness or a burning sensation) occurs, stop using it immediately and consult a doctor or pharmacist.

groups.title: Tablet (E17900ATB)
groups.efficacy: This is an over-the-counter medicine used for the relief of headache, toothache, pain after a tooth extraction, sore throat, earache, joint pain, neuralgia, back pain, muscle pain, stiff shoulders, bruising pain, fracture pain, sprain pain, menstrual pain (period pain) and pain from injury, and to bring down fever when there are chills and a raised temperature.
groups.usage: Adults and those aged 15 years and over: take 1 tablet at a time, 1 to 3 times in 1 day, avoiding an empty stomach. Leave an interval of at least 4 hours between doses.
groups.caution:
If you regularly drink three or more glasses of alcohol every day, consult a doctor or pharmacist before taking this medicine or any other antipyretic analgesic. It may cause gastrointestinal bleeding.

Do not take this medicine if you have hypersensitivity to it or have had it; if you have had asthma when taking this medicine or its ingredients, another antipyretic analgesic or a cold medicine; if the user is an infant under 3 months of age; or if you are 30 weeks pregnant or more.
Before taking this medicine, consult a doctor or pharmacist if the user is a child under 2 years of age; if the user is an infant or a child under 15 years of age who has, or is suspected of having, chickenpox or influenza; if you have an allergic constitution; if you are pregnant, may be pregnant or are breast-feeding; if you have had allergic symptoms caused by a medicine, such as fever, rash, joint pain, asthma or itching; or if you are an older person, physically weak or have a high fever.
Before taking this medicine, consult a doctor or pharmacist if you have liver disease, kidney disease, heart disease, thyroid disease, diabetes or high blood pressure; if you have heartburn, stomach discomfort, stomach pain or another stomach problem that lasts or comes back, or an ulcer or a bleeding problem; or if you have lost a lot of body fluid through vomiting and diarrhoea or are unable to take fluid in.
If symptoms do not improve after 5 or 6 doses, stop taking this medicine immediately and consult a doctor or pharmacist.
Do not keep taking it over a long period.
Keep to the stated dosage and schedule.

Do not take other antipyretic analgesics, cold medicines or sedatives while you are taking this medicine.
Before taking this medicine, consult a doctor or pharmacist if you are receiving medicines for diabetes, gout or arthritis, anticoagulants, steroids or diuretics.
Do not drink alcohol when you take it.

If rash and reddening, itching, nausea and vomiting, loss of appetite, constipation, bleeding from the digestive tract, stomach discomfort, dizziness or oedema (swelling) occurs, stop taking this medicine immediately and consult a doctor or pharmacist.
Rarely, shock (anaphylaxis) — with hives, swelling and tightness of the chest appearing immediately after a dose, together with pallor, cold hands and feet, cold sweat and difficulty breathing — or drug reaction with eosinophilia and systemic symptoms (DRESS syndrome), Stevens-Johnson syndrome, toxic epidermal necrolysis (Lyell's syndrome) or asthma may occur; if so, stop taking this medicine immediately and consult a doctor or pharmacist.
Very rarely erythema multiforme, exfoliative dermatitis or acute generalised exanthematous pustulosis, and at an unknown frequency Kounis syndrome, may occur; if so, stop taking this medicine immediately and consult a doctor or pharmacist.

groups.title: Capsule (E25900ACH)
groups.efficacy: This is an over-the-counter medicine used for cough and phlegm.
groups.usage: Adults and those aged 15 years and over: take 2 capsules at a time, 3 times in 1 day, after meals.
groups.caution:
Do not take this medicine if you have hypersensitivity to it, if the user is an infant under 3 months of age or a child under 2 years of age, or if you have a hereditary problem such as galactose intolerance, Lapp lactase deficiency or glucose-galactose malabsorption.
Before taking this medicine, consult a doctor or pharmacist if the user is a child under 2 years of age and it is genuinely needed; if you are pregnant, may be pregnant or are breast-feeding; if you are an older person or physically weak; if you have an allergic constitution or have had allergic symptoms (fever, rash, joint pain, asthma, itching and the like); if you have liver disease, kidney disease, heart disease, thyroid disease, diabetes, high blood pressure, glaucoma (eye pain, blurred vision and the like), difficulty passing urine or a high fever; if you smoke, or have asthma, chronic bronchitis, emphysema, a cough with a lot of phlegm, a cough lasting or coming back for more than 1 week, a chronic cough, or a cough with fever, rash or a persistent headache; or if you have hypersensitivity to Food Yellow No. 5 or have had it.
Keep to the stated dosage and schedule.
When it is given to a child, give it under the guidance and supervision of a guardian.
Drowsiness may occur after a dose, so be careful when driving or operating machinery.
If there is no improvement in symptoms after 5 or 6 doses, stop taking it immediately and consult a doctor or pharmacist.

Do not take it together with MAO inhibitors (antidepressants, antipsychotics, mood stabilisers, anti-Parkinson medicines and the like), other cough and expectorant medicines, cold medicines, oral medicines containing antihistamines (oral medicines for rhinitis, travel sickness medicines, allergy medicines) or sedatives.
Do not take this medicine if you stopped taking an MAO inhibitor (antidepressant, antipsychotic, mood stabiliser, anti-Parkinson medicine and the like) within the last 2 weeks.
Do not drink alcohol while you are taking it.

If rash, reddening, itching, nausea, vomiting, loss of appetite, dizziness, difficulty passing urine, thirst (persistent or severe), anxiety, tremor or insomnia occurs, stop taking it immediately and consult a doctor or pharmacist.
